meta.title: Android Device Discovery & Live Mirroring (F-2) — Implementation Plan

data.goal: Make every static stub in the merged F-1 shell live for Android: detect adb/idb at launch and show per-platform status, offer a full-stage device picker over Physical + Emulator sources with inline Boot and arrow/Enter navigation, start a live mirror on the selected device through a swappable MirrorTransport, show the passive NO SIGNAL state while adb reports nothing, and report honest tool/resolution/fps/latency stats in the status bar — with zero new dependencies, all adb/idb execution confined to one internal desktopMain file behind a device-scoped API, and v1's NFR-1 latency shortfall carried as an explicit, measured waiver rather than a silent miss.
data.problemStatement: Rectify's canonical window exists (F-1) but shows nothing real: the platform switch, device indicator, and status bar are static previews, and StageSurface has no content source. Until a real Android device can be discovered and mirrored inside the single canonical window, there is no product to annotate — every downstream spec (annotation, measurement, payload, error recovery) depends on this one being live.
data.highLevelDescription: One vertical slice through the existing data → domain → presentation layering, with process execution quarantined in a single desktop-only module. Three new Gradle modules (data-device-api, data-device-impl, presentation-feature-mirror) join the existing 24, and five existing modules are amended (domain-core, domain-repository-api, domain-usecase-api, domain-usecase-impl, data-repository-impl, presentation-core-ui, presentation-core-localisation, compose-application). Every pure parser — adb devices -l, wm size, wm density, emulator -list-avds, the foldable PNG-signature trim, the adb argv builder and the tool-probe candidate order — lives in data-device-api's commonMain, which is the single decision that makes AC-2/AC-3/AC-41/AC-42/AC-44 verifiable with plain kotlin.test and no phone attached (AS-7). java.lang.ProcessBuilder appears in exactly one internal file in data-device-impl/desktopMain. The mirror is a MirrorTransport interface whose v1 implementation is an adaptive single-flight adb exec-out screencap -p loop; the picker, the NO SIGNAL stage and the stats line are Orbit MVI state in presentation-feature-mirror, injected by RectifyWindow and passed as plain data into RectifyShellContent, which stays Koin/AWT/coroutine-free.
data.background: F-1 (app-shell-window-layout) shipped and merged to development (merge commit 62808cc, verdict complete-with-waivers). It delivered RectifyWindowShell, ShellToolbar (six fixed named slots), ShellStatusBar (leading/trailing), StageSurface (bezel-less stage + dot grid, required content slot), SidePanelFrame, ShellState/ShellTab/ShellWindowDefaults, and RectifyShellContent with every slot filled by a static stub. It also shipped ~109 kit components, among them SourceListRow/SourceListHeader, SegmentedButtonGroup, DeviceChip, StatusIndicator, AppButton, KeyCap, SectionHeader, StatusPill, CommandBlock and ErrorCard — the chrome F-3 will need. rectify-poc's Devices.kt (249 lines) is a reference implementation only: its logic (adb devices -l parsing, screencap with the foldable trim, wm size/density/getprop) is proven and portable; its flat structure, untyped error() calls and blocking threads are not. Stage 1 closed with readyForPlan: true and twelve binding decisions, including a recorded NFR-1 waiver approved under survey option B — flagged for re-review before ship.

assumptions: AS-6: scrcpy 3.3.1 and adb remain available via PATH/Homebrew-standard locations during implementation and demo; detection reads the environment dynamically rather than hardcoding this machine's verified paths.

AS-7: no physical device or running emulator is guaranteed in the build/test environment; AC-2/AC-3/AC-41/AC-42/AC-44 'test' verification is achieved by exercising pure parsers and fake sources, never real hardware.

AS-8: shipping screenshot polling as the v1 transport (not meeting NFR-1) is an accepted, explicitly-flagged trade-off, approved at the Stage 1 gate under option B — carried forward here, not resolved.

AS-9: SourceListRow is the picker's row component; the only change it needs is one additive optional parameter — confirmed by reading the file (it already has radio + mono serial + trailing slot and a preview showing all three comp states).

VERIFIED (not assumed): decodeToImageBitmap is reachable from a feature module's commonMain — FeatureConventionPlugin line 115 wires composeDependencies.components.resources into commonMain, which is where org.jetbrains.compose.resources.decodeToImageBitmap lives. No new dependency; the skiko desktopMain fallback is not needed.

VERIFIED (not assumed): kotlinx-coroutines-test is genuinely wired, not merely cataloged — data-preference-impl/build.gradle.kts declares it in its commonTest block today, so virtual-time testing of the 2s poller needs only the same one line in the new modules.
VERIFIED (not assumed): kotlin.test is supplied to commonTest by both LibraryConventionPlugin and FeatureConventionPlugin, so no new module needs to declare it.

Koin single definitions resolve lazily at injection time, so data-group ordering inside initKoin is defensive rather than load-bearing — but the repo rule treats order as significant, so dataDeviceImplModule is placed before its consumer dataRepositoryImplModule anyway.
A frame's ByteArray is wrapped, never copied, when crossing the resource→model boundary — the per-frame allocation is one small object, not a pixel buffer.

constraints.text: Zero new runtime or test dependencies. Everything used is JDK, kotlinx-coroutines, Compose Multiplatform, Koin or kotlin.test — all already wired. The only dependency this spec would otherwise need (a JVM H.264 decoder) is precisely what FR-24 defers.
All adb/idb process execution routes through one device-scoped command executor whose API requires a resolved DeviceId; no repository, use case or composable may shell out directly (NFR-5, AC-44).

Kotlin daemon is capped at 3GB in gradle.properties; building three new KMP modules across all targets at once OOMs the 18GB host. Build one module per implementation step; never ./gradlew build at the root.

explicitApi() is enforced repo-wide — every public declaration needs an explicit visibility modifier AND an explicit return type. core/ is internal-only, source/ is public; a module with no internal declarations gets no core/ directory.
Design tokens only: no literal Color(0x…), no raw .dp at a call site, no hardcoded TextStyle. Strict atom → molecule → organism direction in presentation-core-ui.

A commonTest backtick function name containing a comma or an apostrophe compiles on the JVM and fails compileTestKotlinIosArm64 — F-1 shipped that bug repo-wide. Plain-word backtick names only, no punctuation at all, and one iOS test-compile before the slice is declared done.
DeviceCommand is a closed sealed set, not a vararg string runner — argument injection and remote targets are unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.
RectifyShellContent must gain zero Koin, AWT and coroutine imports; every new parameter is plain data with a default so the F-1 render harness keeps compiling and driving it from literals.
PRD estimates this spec as 'L'; the staged transport (FR-24) keeps it inside that envelope by deferring the highest-cost item rather than absorbing it.
The measurement step (step 12) is a gate, not a nicety: the v1 capture rate and per-frame latency must be real numbers written into the delivery notes before the slice is called done.

risks.text: Screenshot polling delivers roughly 3–7 fps and ~250–500 ms per frame, so the mirror feels like a slideshow under drag and NFR-1 is visibly unmet in the demo.
risks.mitigation: An accepted, recorded waiver (FR-24/AS-8), re-flagged at the Stage 1 gate under option B. Keep fps honest, keep latency an explicit placeholder (AC-45), add the one-word 'polling' hint next to fps, and keep MirrorTransport to two members so the decoder transport is a new class plus one DI line.

risks.text: PATH in a packaged macOS .app omits /opt/homebrew/bin, so adb detection works all through development and fails the first time anyone double-clicks the app.
risks.mitigation: probeCandidates() is a PURE function in data-device-api/commonMain returning the ordered candidate list from an injected env map and home dir; ToolResolver only applies an executable predicate to it. Unit-tested with a fake env (empty PATH, ANDROID_HOME set, Homebrew-only) and every path tried is recorded in ToolProbe.probedPaths for F-3's comp-04 footer.

risks.text: Orphaned adb children after an abrupt window close hold the USB connection and make the next launch see no device.
risks.mitigation: Live-child registry (Collections.newSetFromMap(ConcurrentHashMap())) + one Runtime shutdown hook registered once + destroyForcibly() in finally + a per-call withTimeoutOrNull budget. The adb server daemon itself is never killed.

risks.text: Three new modules plus edits to eight existing ones blow the 3GB Kotlin daemon when built together.
risks.mitigation: The implementation sequence is bottom-up and per-module; each step names its own single :module:build or :module:desktopTest command. No root build at any point.

risks.text: A commonTest backtick name containing a comma or apostrophe compiles on JVM and breaks compileTestKotlinIosArm64 — this spec adds more test files than any before it.
risks.mitigation: Plain-word backtick names, no punctuation. Step 13 runs ./gradlew :data-device-api:compileTestKotlinIosArm64 :presentation-feature-mirror:compileTestKotlinIosArm64 before the slice is declared done.

risks.text: Frames pushed through the Orbit reducer at up to 10/s cause allocation churn and sluggish UI that gets misdiagnosed as transport latency.
risks.mitigation: Pixels live in a dedicated StateFlow<ImageBitmap?> outside Orbit state; only semantic state goes through the reducer, and stats update on a separate 1s ticker rather than per frame.

risks.text: The live mirror repaints over StageSurface's dot grid, whose Canvas draws every dot across the full stage on each pass (F-1 review finding PRF-1, unverified) — at 10fps that cost is paid 10x/second behind an opaque image.
risks.mitigation: MirrorFrameView is aspect-fit and opaque where it covers; measure frame time in step 12 alongside the capture rate and, if the grid shows up, raise it as a scoped PRF-1 follow-up in presentation-core-ui rather than fixing it inline here.

risks.text: Adding Failure.Technical.Process to a sealed hierarchy in the zero-dependency core breaks exhaustive when expressions elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: Grep `is Failure.Technical` and `when (failure)` before the change; nothing branches exhaustively today. Build :domain-core then :domain-usecase-impl first (step 1).

risks.text: Orbit's internal intent dispatching makes plain runTest assertions over container.stateFlow flaky, tempting an orbit-test dependency that is not in the catalog.
risks.mitigation: Dispatchers.setMain(StandardTestDispatcher) + advanceUntilIdle() before each assertion; if that proves unreliable, fall back to covering the extracted pure helpers (nextSelectableIndex, discovery→state derivation, stats formatting) and keep VM coverage at smoke level. Adding orbit-test is an open question for a gate, never a quiet fix.

risks.text: Unauthorized/offline devices are filtered out (the poc's behaviour), so a user with a plugged-in phone sees NO SIGNAL and follows guidance that cannot help them.
risks.mitigation: parseAdbDevices returns a typed DeviceStateResource for every entry; non-`device` states survive into DeviceModel and render as non-selectable rows with their state as the trailing label (SourceListRow gains `enabled`). Arrow keys skip them.

risks.text: scrcpy 3.3.1 is installed on the dev machine and will tempt a 'just shell out to scrcpy' shortcut, opening a second OS window and breaking F-1's canonical-window contract.
risks.mitigation: The closed DeviceCommand set contains no scrcpy command and the host sources enumerate only adb/emulator subcommands; adding one is a visible, reviewable API change in data-device-api, not a one-line call site.

risks.text: Pre-existing repo hazard made live by this spec: resultLauncher catches Throwable, which includes CancellationException, so a withTimeout inside any use case would swallow genuine parent-scope cancellation.
risks.mitigation: This spec uses withTimeoutOrNull everywhere and never lets a TimeoutCancellationException reach resultLauncher. Fixing the helper itself (adding `catch (c: CancellationException) { throw c }`) touches every existing use case and is explicitly flagged as a separate follow-up, not done here.

risks.text: Picker key handling and the window-level Cmd+1/2/3 handler fight over focus once the side panel exists in a later spec.
risks.mitigation: Ownership splits by modifier: unmodified keys belong to the focused panel, meta-modified keys to the window. handleShellShortcut is untouched, and a VM test asserts arrow/Enter intents carry no meta semantics.

functional.text: On launch, detect installed adb and idb tool versions and show a status dot per platform in the toolbar.
Show a platform switch (Android/iOS) in the toolbar on every screen; Android is functional in v1, iOS is deferred to v1.1+.
Provide a device picker dropdown with Physical-device and Emulator sections (running, or shut-down with an inline Boot button), navigable via arrow keys and Enter.
Provide a primary 'Start mirroring' action that connects to the selected device and begins the live mirror stream.
When no device is connected, poll adb every 2s and show a 'NO SIGNAL' empty state with guidance to plug in a USB-debug device or boot an emulator inline.
Show a status bar with live stream stats: tool version, resolution, fps, and latency.

v1 ships a screenshot-polling mirror transport (adb exec-out screencap, reusing rectify-poc's proven capture/foldable-trim logic) as the FR-4 stream source; it is explicitly documented as not meeting NFR-1's <150ms target. An H.264-decode transport (scrcpy-server socket consumed in-JVM) is a deliberate v1.1+ follow-up, gated on choosing and justifying a new JVM decoder dependency per version-catalog-hygiene.md.

The live mirror transport is abstracted behind a single interface consumed by StageSurface's content slot and by FR-22's stats contract, so swapping the v1 polling transport for a future decoder-based transport (FR-24) requires no change to the shell integration or the stats shape.

nonFunctional.text: Live mirror glass-to-glass latency should stay low enough (target under ~150ms) that drag-to-select and freeze feel responsive. WAIVED FOR v1 — screenshot polling knowingly misses this; the real achieved number must be measured (step 12) and recorded, and the waiver is flagged for re-review before ship.

adb/idb commands are only ever invoked against the user's explicitly selected, connected device — never an arbitrary or remote target. Enforced by API shape (see security section), not by call-site discipline.

Device picker, annotation popovers, and error-card actions are fully keyboard-navigable (arrow keys/Enter for pickers, Enter/Escape for popovers). In F-2's scope: the picker and the NO SIGNAL emulator control.
v1 targets macOS only; no Windows/Linux builds. The desktop actual is the only functional one; android/iOS actuals register unsupported sources so common code still compiles on all four targets.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given adb and idb are installed, when the app launches, then the toolbar shows a status dot reflecting detected tool versions for both platforms.
Given a physical device is connected and an emulator is running, when the device picker is opened, then both appear in distinct Physical/Emulator sections and arrow keys plus Enter select an entry.
Given a device is selected in the picker, when the user clicks 'Start mirroring', then the live mirror begins streaming.
Given no device is connected, when adb polling runs, then the 'NO SIGNAL' state shows with guidance text and an inline emulator picker plus Boot button.
Given live mirror is active, then the status bar displays current tool version, resolution, fps, and latency, updating at least once per second.

Given adb is not found on PATH at launch, when tool detection runs, then F-2 exposes a typed ToolMissing discovery state (and reflects it as an offline/warning toolbar status dot) for error-handling-and-recovery (F-3) to render as the actionable error card (comp 04) — F-2 itself does not build the Locate-adb/Retry/Copy UI.

Given adb is installed but reports zero attached devices across repeated polls, when polling runs, then F-2 exposes a typed NoDeviceFound discovery state carrying poll metadata (last-poll time, attempt count) for F-3 to render the escalated error card (comp 05, Restart adb / Boot emulator instead) — F-2's own stage still shows only the passive NO SIGNAL state from AC-4.

Given no device has ever been selected, when the app has focus, then the device picker renders as a centered panel filling the stage's content slot on Theme.color.bg (not the dotted stage background), matching comps 01/03; given a device is already selected, clicking the toolbar DeviceChip reopens the same panel. There is no separate small anchored dropdown menu implementation.

Given any adb/idb command needs to run, then it is issued only through the single device-scoped command executor, whose API requires an already-resolved device id as a non-optional parameter — no code path in the codebase can construct or issue a device command without one (NFR-5 enforced by API shape).

Given live mirror is active, then the status bar shows tool version and resolution unconditionally, fps reflecting the active transport's real achieved rate, and latency either as a real measurement or an explicit placeholder (never a fabricated number) when the active transport cannot measure it end-to-end — all updating at least once per second.

architecture.approach: One vertical slice through the existing data → domain → presentation layering, with process execution quarantined in one desktop-only module and every pure function hoisted into commonMain so it is testable without hardware. Three new modules: data-device-api (contracts + ALL parsers, library+di), data-device-impl (the only ProcessBuilder in the repo, desktopMain-only and internal, behind an internal expect fun Module.provideDeviceSources() copying data-preference-impl's provideSettings() pattern exactly), and presentation-feature-mirror (Orbit MVI, entry point MirrorHost rather than *Screen because this surface is a shell slot set, not a navigation destination). data-repository-impl gains DeviceRepositoryImpl with the 2s polling flow and the empty-poll escalation; domain-core gains the device model vocabulary and Failure.Technical.Process; five use cases follow the existing one-interface-one-invoke shape. The mirror itself is a two-member MirrorTransport interface, so the v1.1+ decoder transport is a new class plus one DI line.
architecture.rationale: Every decision was taken against two filters: does it make a claim true by construction (type system, module boundary, API shape) rather than by convention, and does it stay proportional to a PRD 'L' estimate for discovery plus first connection. Putting the parsers in data-device-api/commonMain is what converts AS-7 ('no phone in CI') from an aspiration into a structural fact. Putting ProcessBuilder behind internal + a module boundary + explicitApi() is what makes NFR-5 unbreakable rather than merely documented. Hoisting probeCandidates() out of ToolResolver into a pure commonMain function is what makes the highest-likelihood, highest-impact risk in the spec (the packaged-.app PATH failure) unit-testable with a fake env map. Keeping pixels in a StateFlow outside Orbit state is what stops every future annotation feature inheriting a reducer pass per frame. Reuse was preferred everywhere the kit allowed: eight shipped components are used as-is, one gains a single additive parameter, and only six new UI pieces are authored — each justified below.

alternativesConsidered.title: One combined data-device module holding both interfaces and implementation
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: data-repository-impl would have to depend on an impl module (no other slice in the repo does), tests would pull the desktop process code onto the classpath, and the api/impl symmetry that preferences and database already establish would break. Saves one build file, costs the structural guarantee that is the entire point of NFR-5.

alternativesConsidered.title: Put the mirror ViewModel in compose-application/desktopMain next to its only consumer
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: compose-application/CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids feature logic and ViewModels there, Orbit and koin-viewmodel are not wired into that module, and desktopMain placement would make the state machine untestable from commonTest. Violating a written module rule to save one build.gradle.kts is not a trade.

alternativesConsidered.title: Reuse Failure.Technical.Platform for process failures
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Platform is documented as Android/iOS OS-level errors — the mobile runtime, not a host CLI. F-3 must distinguish 'adb missing' from 'adb failed' to choose comp 04 vs comp 05, and would be reduced to string-matching messages. Cheaper today, ambiguous forever.

alternativesConsidered.title: Fixed-interval capture timer (fire every 100ms regardless of completion)
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Stacks overlapping adb processes the moment a capture exceeds the interval — the exact failure that hangs USB and spawns orphans — and would make the status bar report the requested rate rather than the achieved one, violating AC-45.

alternativesConsidered.title: Launch scrcpy as a child process
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: It opens its own OS window and therefore cannot composite into StageSurface at all, breaking F-1's canonical-window contract. Structurally prevented here: the closed DeviceCommand set contains no scrcpy command.

alternativesConsidered.title: Route picker keys through RectifyWindow's existing onPreviewKeyEvent
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: The window would have to know whether the picker is open and which row is highlighted, pushing feature state into the shell; and preview dispatch runs root-first, so the window would start intercepting arrow keys from every future focused control.

alternativesConsidered.title: Push decoded frames through the Orbit reducer as part of MirrorUiState
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Up to 10 reducer passes and 10 full state copies per second, inherited by every downstream annotation feature. Pixels are a stream; UI semantics are a state machine.

alternativesConsidered.title: Add orbit-test and/or turbine to make ViewModel tests ergonomic
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Two new dependencies for test ergonomics against a hard zero-new-dependency constraint. runTest + Dispatchers.setMain + advanceUntilIdle covers it; if it proves flaky the fallback is extracting more pure helpers, and adding the dependency would be a gated decision with a version-catalog-hygiene justification.

alternativesConsidered.title: A separate small anchored dropdown for the toolbar DeviceChip, in addition to the full-stage panel
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: AC-43 settles it: one panel, reopened from the chip. Two picker implementations would be two things to keep in sync for one user intention.

components.name: DeviceId
components.responsibility: data-device-api/src/commonMain/kotlin/data/device/api/source/model/DeviceId.kt — @JvmInline value class with a PRIVATE constructor and a `public fun of(raw: String): DeviceId?` factory rejecting blank, whitespace-bearing, leading-dash and non-[A-Za-z0-9._:-] input. architecture.stateManagement: Orbit MVI in presentation-feature-mirror for UI semantics (MirrorContract/MirrorViewModel/MirrorContent + MirrorHost in place of the usual *Screen — a documented deviation, since this surface is a slot set rather than a navigation destination). Pixels deliberately bypass Orbit: MirrorViewModel decodes each PNG on Dispatchers.Default via decodeToImageBitmap() and publishes to a `public val frame: StateFlow<ImageBitmap?>` outside the reduced state, so up to 10 frames/second never become 10 reducer passes and 10 state copies. Stats are reduced on a separate 1s ticker, not per frame. The 2s discovery cadence lives in DeviceRepositoryImpl's flow, not in a ViewModel timer; session switching is flatMapLatest over the selected device, so rapid Start/Stop can never leave two capture loops alive. Lifetime is structural: window close → ViewModel cleared → viewModelScope cancelled → delay cancels → finally destroys children. Shell state (active tab, panel width) stays in F-1's ShellState, untouched.
navigation: No Destination is added and NavigationHost is not touched — the desktop root is RectifyWindow, not the navigation graph, and this surface is a set of shell slots (the documented reason the entry point is MirrorHost, not MirrorScreen).

Stage content is a state branch, not a route: DevicePickerPanel when isPickerOpen, NoSignalStage when discovery is ToolMissing/NoDeviceFound/empty Found, MirrorFrameView while a session streams, and a deferred-platform notice when the switch is on iOS.
The toolbar DeviceChip reopens the same picker panel (AC-43); Escape closes it only when a device is already selected.
F-1's window-level Cmd+1/2/3 handler (handleShellShortcut) is unmodified; the picker owns unmodified keys only.

errorStates.behavior: DiscoveryModel.Detecting on launch: StatusIndicator(Offline, 'Detecting tools…'), DeviceChip(None), stage shows the picker panel with the PLATFORM cards in a probing state and an empty SOURCE list. No spinner over the stage — detection is sub-second and a flash of chrome is worse than nothing.

DiscoveryModel.NoDeviceFound or Found with no selectable device: NoSignalStage on the dotted stage (dashed outline, 'Waiting for an Android device', the two numbered steps, EmulatorSelect + Boot, 'adb devices · polling every 2 s'), StatusIndicator(Standby, 'Waiting for device…'), DeviceChip(None). Polling continues every 2s; a device appearing switches the stage without user action (AC-4, SC-2).
Zero AVDs installed: EmulatorSelect renders disabled with an explanatory label rather than opening an empty menu, and the Boot button is disabled alongside it.

DiscoveryModel.ToolMissing: StatusIndicator(Offline, 'adb not found'), the Android PlatformToolCard shows an offline dot and 'not found', and the typed state (with probedPaths and installCommand) is published for F-3. F-2 renders no Locate/Retry/Copy UI (AC-41, SC-6).

Sustained empty polls: the stage keeps the passive NO SIGNAL state while NoDeviceFound(toolVersion, lastPollEpochMs, attempts, attachedCount) is published for F-3's escalated card. F-2 never escalates its own stage (AC-42, SC-7).

Unauthorized or offline device attached: the row appears in the picker as non-selectable (SourceListRow enabled = false) with its state as the trailing label, arrow keys skip it, and the user is not told 'no device' while holding one.

Failure.Technical.Process during a session (device vanished, non-zero exit, timeout, hung child): the session ends cleanly, DeviceChip flips to Lost, the stage returns to NO SIGNAL, and 2s discovery resumes. Reconnect UX is F-3's.

Failure.Technical.Process during a one-shot (boot, detect, device info): a MirrorSideEffect.ShowError is posted and the previous state is kept; detection re-derives on the next poll. An already-running AVD's lock-file exit is treated as a no-op success, not an error.

Platform switch moved to iOS: any Android session stops immediately, the stage shows a deferred-platform notice built from existing kit text styles, and the iOS PlatformToolCard still shows the detected idb probe (FR-2).

logs: Kermit Logger.withTag("ToolResolver") at info once per launch: which tool resolved, at which path, after how many candidates — the single most useful line when a packaged .app misbehaves.
Logger.withTag("DeviceDiscovery") at debug on state TRANSITION only (Detecting→Found, Found→NoDeviceFound, attach/detach), never once per 2s poll — a poll that changes nothing logs nothing.
Logger.withTag("MirrorSession") at info on session start and stop with the device id and frame dimensions; at warn on Failure.Technical.Process with argv, exit code and the capped stderr tail.
Logger.withTag("ScreencapTransport") at debug once per 1s stats tick with achieved fps and cumulative dropped frames — never per frame.
No log line ever contains frame bytes, and the stderr tail is capped at MirrorTuning.StderrTailBytes (2KB) so a chatty tool cannot balloon a log.
metrics: TransportStats.fps — achieved frames per second over the trailing 1s window (the number AC-45 requires to be real).
TransportStats.droppedFrames — cumulative captures skipped by the single-flight guard; the honest signal that the device is slower than the floor.
TransportStats.latencyMs — null for the polling transport; rendered as an explicit placeholder, never a fabricated number.
DiscoveryModel.NoDeviceFound.attempts and lastPollEpochMs — poll metadata, also F-3's comp-05 footer data.
ToolProbe.probedPaths.size — how many candidates were tried before resolution; feeds F-3's comp-04 footer.
Measured once in step 12 and recorded in the delivery notes, not emitted at runtime: per-frame capture round-trip (ms), decode time (ms), and end-to-end observed latency.

accessibility.requirement: NFR-8 / AC-2: the device picker is fully operable from the keyboard — ↑/↓ move the highlight, Enter activates it, and nothing in the picker requires a pointer.

Arrow keys skip non-selectable rows (unauthorized, offline, no-permissions) rather than landing on a row Enter cannot act on; the highlight clamps at the first and last selectable rows rather than wrapping silently.
Enter on a shut-down emulator row Boots it rather than starting a mirror — there is nothing to mirror yet — and the keyboard hint reflects the highlighted row's actual action.
Escape closes the picker only when a device is already selected; on first run there is nothing behind the panel, so Escape is an explicit no-op rather than an empty stage.
The panel requests focus when it appears (FocusRequester in a LaunchedEffect) and returns focus to the stage when it closes, so keyboard control is never stranded.
Device rows carry Role.RadioButton semantics (already true of SourceListRow) and a non-selectable row is announced as disabled, not merely dimmed.
Status is never conveyed by colour alone: every status dot is paired with its text (adb 35.0.1, not found, Running, Waiting for device…), as the comps already show.
MirrorFrameView carries a contentDescription naming the mirrored device, so the stage is not an unlabelled image.

performanceBudget.target: 2000 ms exactly, from MirrorTuning.DiscoveryPollMs; the interval is between poll completions, so a slow adb cannot stack polls.

performanceBudget.metric: Host command timeout (adb version, adb devices -l, device info)
performanceBudget.target: 3000 ms via withTimeoutOrNull; a timeout yields Failure.Technical.Process, never a swallowed cancellation. Covers adb's 1–3s cold-start daemon case, which must not read as a failure.

100 ms minimum between capture issues (MirrorTuning.CaptureFloorMs) — a 10 fps ceiling. The loop is adaptive: it re-issues as soon as the previous frame is decoded, so the floor only bites on a fast device.
5000 ms (MirrorTuning.CaptureTimeoutMs); the child is destroyForcibly()'d in finally and the frame is counted as dropped.
Exactly 1. A capture still running when the next issue is due increments TransportStats.droppedFrames instead of spawning a second adb child.

performanceBudget.metric: Expected achieved capture rate (v1 polling transport)
performanceBudget.target: 3–7 fps and ~250–500 ms per frame on a 1080p device over USB — AN ESTIMATE CARRIED FROM BRAINSTORM. Step 12 replaces it with a measured number plus the device model, resolution and link type; the MirrorTuning floor is then justified against that measurement.

< 40 ms per 1080p frame on Dispatchers.Default; measured in step 12 alongside the capture rate. Decode never runs on the Compose/AWT thread, so a slow decode drops the frame rate but never freezes the window.

<150 ms is the requirement and v1 KNOWINGLY DOES NOT MEET IT. The polling transport cannot even measure it end-to-end, so TransportStats.latencyMs is null and the status bar shows an explicit placeholder (AC-45). The waiver is recorded and flagged for re-review before ship.
Exactly 1000 ms (MirrorTuning.StatsTickMs) — 'at least once per second' satisfied by a dedicated ticker, decoupled from the frame rate so a 3 fps stream still updates its stats 1/s.

Tool version and resolution unconditionally; resolution read from the CURRENT frame so rotation is followed rather than cached at connect time; fps = achieved rate; a one-word 'polling' hint next to fps; latency as '—'. Dropped frames are carried in the model but not shown in v1's status bar.

performanceBudget.metric: Orbit reducer passes per second while streaming
performanceBudget.target: ≤ 1 for stats plus whatever semantic events occur — never one per frame. Frames reach the UI through a StateFlow<ImageBitmap?> outside the reduced state.
Zero orphaned adb children after an abrupt window close (live-child registry + one shutdown hook + destroyForcibly in finally). The adb server daemon is never killed.
The seven :desktopTest tasks complete in well under a minute on a warm daemon — all pure JVM, no Compose UI harness, no device, no real process spawned.

dataHandling: NFR-5 is enforced by API shape at five independent points, any one of which would have to be deliberately dismantled to break it: (1) DeviceId is a value class with a PRIVATE constructor whose only factory, DeviceId.of(raw), rejects blank, whitespace-bearing, leading-dash and out-of-charset input — an arbitrary string cannot become a device id; (2) DeviceCommand is a CLOSED sealed set of five cases with no vararg, no free-text and no scrcpy member, so there is no 'run this string' API anywhere in the dependency graph and argument injection is not a category that exists; (3) DeviceCommandExecutor has exactly one method and one overload, run(device: DeviceId, command: DeviceCommand) — the device parameter is non-optional and cannot be defaulted; (4) buildDeviceArgv is the single argv construction point in the repository and always emits [adbPath, "-s", device.value, …], asserted by a test over every DeviceCommand variant (AC-44); (5) ProcessRunner is internal, lives in data-device-impl/src/desktopMain, and is unreachable from any other module by the combination of module boundary, internal, and explicitApi().

Remote targets are unrepresentable rather than merely forbidden: adb connect, -H and -P have no DeviceCommand case and no AdbHostSource method, so no code path can address a device over the network. Adding one would be a visible, reviewable change to a public sealed hierarchy in data-device-api.

The deviceless surface (adb --version, adb devices -l, emulator -list-avds, emulator -avd) is enumerated on two separate interfaces precisely so that 'this command has no device' is an auditable exception with five named members, rather than a nullable parameter on the device executor that every future call site could pass null to.
Frame bytes live only in memory, are never written to disk or a temp file in v1, and are released as soon as the next frame replaces them. Nothing in this spec persists a screenshot.

Process stderr is captured for diagnostics but capped at 2KB (MirrorTuning.StderrTailBytes) before it enters DeviceCommandException, so a chatty or hostile tool cannot flood a log or a Failure message.
Stage 5 inspection, not just a test: grep the repository for ProcessBuilder and for `-s` argv construction, and assert exactly one file matches each.
permissions: No new OS permissions. The app reads environment variables (ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, HOME, PATH), checks file executability on the probed candidate paths, and spawns the user's own adb/emulator binaries — all ordinary user-level operations on macOS.

USB debugging authorisation stays entirely with the device and adb; Rectify never bypasses or suppresses the on-device prompt, and an unauthorized device is surfaced as a non-selectable row with its real state.
privacy: A mirrored screen can contain anything the user has on their phone. v1 keeps frames in memory only, ships no telemetry, and emits no analytics event (there is no analytics layer in this repo at all).
Log lines never contain frame data, and device serials appear only in local debug logs — never transmitted anywhere, because nothing in this spec transmits.
ToolProbe.probedPaths contains local filesystem paths and is exposed to F-3 for the comp-04 diagnostics footer; that is on-screen local diagnostics for the user's own machine, not data leaving it.
